rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ❌ Dark matter is the same as dark energy. ✅ Dark matter (27%) is a form of mass that exerts gravitational attraction — it clumps and forms structure. Dark energy (68%) is a property of space itself that causes accelerated expansion and does not clump. They are fundamentally different.  ·  ❌ Black holes suck in everything around them. ✅ Outside the event horizon, black holes behave like any other object of the same mass. A black hole's gravity at the distance of Earth's orbit is identical to the Sun's. Black holes are dangerous only if you get very close.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: ❌ Nothing can escape from inside a black hole, not even light. ✅ This is the DEFINITION of an event horizon. Nothing, not even light, can escape once inside $R_s$. This is why they are called black holes.  ·  ❌ Gravitational waves are made of matter. ✅ Gravitational waves are ripples in SPACETIME ITSELF — not made of any material substance. They propagate through empty space at the speed of light, carrying energy.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: The 2017 Nobel Prize in Physics was awarded to Rainer Weiss, Barry Barish, and Kip Thorne for LIGO's detection of gravitational waves — confirming a prediction Einstein made in 1916 and opening a completely new window on the universe.  ·  The Event Horizon Telescope (2019) imaged the black hole shadow in M87, showing a ring of radio emission surrounding a dark center. The image matched general relativistic predictions to high precision, confirming black hole properties predicted by Einstein's theory.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: **Dark matter:** A form of matter that does not emit, absorb, or reflect electromagnetic radiation — it is completely invisible to all telescopes. Its presence is inferred solely from gravitational effects on visible matter, light, and the large-scale structure of the universe. Dark matter comprises approximately 27% of the universe's total energy density.  ·  **Evidence for dark matter — galaxy rotation curves:** Stars in spiral galaxies orbit the galactic center. Newtonian mechanics predicts orbital velocity should decrease with distance from the center ($v \propto 1/\sqrt{r}$). Instead, rotation curves remain FLAT at large radii — stars maintain the same orbital speed far from the visible disk.…  ·  **Evidence — gravitational lensing:** Dark matter bends light from background galaxies through gravitational lensing. The pattern and strength of lensing arcs around galaxy clusters reveal the total mass distribution, which is consistently much larger than the visible mass.…
